summary: Iteration 8 regression — 15/15 pytest cases PASS covering new modules (promotions CRUD + apply with correct discount math, loyalty settings defaults + persistence, audit log sorted desc with user_name/action/description, enhanced /dashboard/summary with today/yesterday/month/prev_month/top10/least_active/chart_14d/alerts/cash_in_drawer/debts, customer+supplier statements w/ opening balance + credit invoices + payment reduction, product kardex movements with running balance, dead-stock, /cashbox/balance+movements, 6 advanced reports) AND regression of core existing endpoints (sales invoice_no increment + stock decrement + return + credit statement, purchases accepting new payment_method+extra_charges with total=subtotal+tax-discount+extra, products accepting new supplier_id/wholesale_price/location AND backward-compatible old-shape creation, customers/suppliers/categories/warehouses/expenses/employees, accounting routes /accounts /journal /vouchers /ledger/{id}). Login as owner@demo.com returns role=owner with shop_id.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2235 lines — split sales/purchases/inventory routes into dedicated modules similar to how promo_loyalty.py and reports_module.py are already extracted.
promo_loyalty._audit swallows all exceptions silently (bare except Exception: pass) — audit failures should at least be logged for traceability.
/promotions/apply stacks all matching active promos additively; this allows unintended double-discounting (e.g., two 10% percent promos on the same cart) — consider priority / exclusivity flag.

reports_module.product_movements loads full purchases/sales/transfers/adjustments collections (to_list(5000)) per request and filters in Python — add an aggregation pipeline with $match on items.product_id and $unwind for scalability.

reports_module._cashbox_calc sums ALL historical sales regardless of date — results drift forever and don't match 'cash in drawer' intuition for shops with long history. Should at minimum be based on current shift or configurable period.

customer_statement/supplier_statement sort entries by date-string (YYYY-MM-DD) but opening balance uses `cust.get('created_at')[:10]` which may be later than historical invoice dates; opening row can end up mid-list — pin opening to sort key '0000-00-00' or explicit ordering.
LoyaltySettingsIn POST silently overwrites all fields with defaults if client omits them (full-replace semantics with no PATCH) — may lose previously-set thresholds; document or switch to PATCH.
No pagination on /audit-log, /promotions, /cashbox/movements — hard limit=200/1000/5000 is server-set but shops with heavy traffic will hit it; add offset/skip.
No role-based protection on destructive endpoints: any shop_user (incl. cashier/accountant) can DELETE promotions, pay/collect from any party, and change loyalty settings — tighten with role checks.
test_credentials: owner@demo.com / Demo@1234 (shop owner), admin@pos.com / Admin@1234 (super admin, not exercised in this iteration).
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates TEST_-prefixed categories/warehouses/suppliers/customers/products/sales/purchases/promotions in the existing demo shop. No cleanup performed (acceptable — prefixed for easy future purge). No new shop was created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini pins each class to a worker with --dist loadscope, so cross-class fixtures do NOT share state. Any end-to-end dependency chain MUST live inside a single class (see TestFullFlow). Promotion /apply stacks all active matching promos — deterministic tests must deactivate pre-existing active promos first. Supplier statement uses credit for purchases and debit for payments (opposite sign to customer statement).
